text:
Nora (People Ops): Quick one  member had an urgent root canal in Madrid and the clinic wants to direct-bill. They also asked we only include CPT and amounts on the EOB when giving a copy to the patient. Claim 2026-INT-8439. Who owns the workflow and what minimal docs do we need to share with the clinic?

Diego (Benefits): Benefits owns coverage review; we require: signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB), patient consent for redaction, itemized invoice with procedure codes and dates, provider tax ID. We cannot remove service dates or codes from our internal record.

Hana (Finance): For international EFT we need IBAN + BIC, beneficiary name exactly as bank record, and a scanned bank mandate if available. Ask if they accept USD to speed payment. Also include a copy of provider's billing license for KYC.

Sam (Legal): On redaction: member can consent to redact identifiers (national ID, SSN, full DOB, address) on the EOB before distribution. We cannot redact service dates or CPT/procedure codes on the EOB that we keep for audit. If provider requests more aggressive redaction, we need a signed waiver and legal review.

Nora (People Ops): Can someone paste a 2-line AOB and a 1-line consent we can ask the member to sign? I want to forward minimal templates to the clinic and member.

Diego (Benefits): AOB (two-line): "I, [MemberName], assign benefits for services related to claim 2026-INT-8439 to [ProviderName] and authorize Redwood Inference to pay the provider directly."

Sam (Legal): Consent (one-line): "I consent to Redwood Inference redacting my national ID, full DOB, and address on the EOB prior to distribution, while leaving service dates, procedure codes, and amounts intact."

Hana (Finance): Provider checklist to forward:
• Signed AOB (PDF)
• Patient consent for redaction (PDF)
• Itemized invoice in EUR (with procedure codes + dates)
• Provider tax/VAT registration
• Banking details: IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, account name; indicate USD acceptance if possible
• Billing contact email/phone
Send to claims@redwood.com and reference Claim 2026-INT-8439.

ClaimsBot: Automated: International direct-bill flagged  manual review required. Expected adjudication 4-10 business days after complete docs received.

Nora (People Ops): Great  I'll email clinic + member with the templates. One more: clinic asked if we can omit member name on the EOB when sending to the patient copy (they think privacy prefers initials). Allowed?

Sam (Legal): We must include member name or initials? Use initials only if member agrees in writing. Best practice: member signs consent and permits initials-only. Document consent in claims file.

Diego (Benefits): Also note: we need service dates on any EOB we send to the provider for reconciliation. Member-facing copy can follow their consent.

Nora (People Ops): Thanks all. Forwarding now and will update when clinic replies. :thumbsup: (End of thread)
